title: Nine Feet of Digging
subtitle: 陶土与泥土 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 陶土与泥土（文学艺术与体育·手工艺与陶艺）
meta: 主题语境：陶土与泥土（文学艺术与体育·手工艺与陶艺）　|　核心词汇：clay　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 clay 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 my mother was sent to dig ① clay she could not shape, and she said the digging was the whole of the lesson. The ② clay, meaning the earth and not the pot, was nine feet down and was dug by whoever came last; clay, she said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ clay in that field had the same colour, and the ④ clay at the end, meaning the one the potter kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever dug properly. Clay, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ clay was the whole of the trade, meaning the vessel it carried and not the earth. The ⑥ clay, meaning the vessel and not any of that, is the only thing in a trade that everybody sells and nobody questions; clay, he said, is either something you dig or the only word that means both earth and a vessel. She said the vessel is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ clay had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the colour. The ⑧ clay of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine feet and eleven years of digging; clay, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ clay I remember is the one at the end, which was dug in 1969 and is still described as the reddest in the county. A ⑩ clay, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being dug; every clay, she said, is a vessel that has agreed to look like earth. She said the vessel was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 陶土（指那些泥土本身，与那只罐子相对）
C. 固定搭配：dig clay 挖陶土
D. n. 陶土（指那片地里每一处）
E. n. 陶土（指末尾那一处）
F. n. 器皿（抽象：它烧成的那只器物）
G. n. 那只器物（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The clay, meaning the earth and not the pot
clay was the whole of the trade
the clay had become a number in a report
The clay of the whole thing
A clay, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: dig clay 意为“挖陶土”，1949 年母亲被派去挖她塑不成形的那处陶土。
clay 意为“黏土、陶土”，指那些泥土本身而不是那只罐子，深九英尺，由最后来的人挖。
clay 指那片地里每一处陶土，每一处都是同样的颜色。
clay 指末尾那一处（陶匠保留的那一处），是唯一有人认真挖过的。
clay 意为“器皿”，抽象指它烧成的那只器物，父亲说 clay 就是那门手艺的全部。
clay 为抽象用法，指那只器物本身，是一门手艺里人人都卖、却没人质疑的东西。
clay 意为“黏土、陶土”，到 1964 年这处 clay 成了报告里的一个数字。
clay 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英尺和十一年的挖掘。
clay 意为“陶土”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1969 年挖过，至今仍被说成全县最红的。
clay 为抽象总称，祖母说一处陶土是唯一会因为被认真挖掘而变好的东西。
